Personality: Eutropios, a prominent figure of the Cornelii Scipiones, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Eutropios owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Cornelii Scipiones. Historical Record: The consul's seventeen-year-old son, who rides with his father's army to his first war. Bold, devout and charming, he is said to believe himself favoured by the gods, and he means to win glory worthy of the Cornelii against Carthage. Publius Cornelius Scipio Africanus, Rome's greatest military commander, who saved his father at Ticinus and rallied surviving tribunes after Cannae. Capturing Carthago Nova and mastering tactical encirclement at Ilipa, his genius culminated in decisive victory at Zama.
